§6Zirconium & Tantalum

§aFuel rod skins and high-end capacitors. One common, one painful to produce.

§6Zirconium§f (atomic 40):
Rare earth metal, high corrosion resistance and melting point. From rare earth ore splinters, cyclotron (strontium + lithium), or depth ore (destroy by explosion to collect).
Uses: §bRBMK fuel rod skins§f (every rod needs it), §bZFB binders§f for breeder rods, PWR fuel and neutron reflectors, ZIRNOX fuel rods.

§6Tantalum§f (atomic 73):
Very rare, produced through a long chain: Find §bcoltan deposit§f (one per 1,000 blocks, use coltass to locate) → shred → chemical plant (purified tantalite) → chemical plant (pandemonium solution) → chemical plant (polycrystal) → shred and smelt. Also from PUREX reprocessing of schrabidium Watz fuel.
Uses: §bTantalum Capacitors§f for bomb control units, quantum computers, and 528 Mode capacitor boards.

§ePS:§f Zirconium is everywhere in reactor fuel. Tantalum is a one-time stockpile, set up the coltan chain and grab enough for your capacitor needs.
